title: Charlie Johnson's Paradise band and Frankie Half-Pint Jackson
summary: He recalls Charlie Johnson's band in Atlantic City and Small's Paradise, Half-Pint Jackson the entertainer, and Johnson leaving the band to play alone.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: But you didn't mention the Charlie Johnson band before, now that was a great band, wasn't it?
Oh, yes.
And that was at the Paradise, wasn't it?
In Atlantic City. They would work in Atlantic City in the summer and the winter they would come here, to Small's Paradise.
Right.
They did that every year.
And let's see, what year was it that you were with Johnson?
That was around '24, '25.
Uh-huh.
Was Frankie Half-Pint Jackson there then?
That's right, that's right.
What was he like, he was very small, right?
Very small, very neat, immaculate fellow.
Uh-huh.

And he could put a song over like you know, nobody in the world could. I'll never forget him. In fact, I do one of his songs now. I started a little singing thing, I do one of his songs now. Every now and then, he was just great. Fact, all the entertainers in those days were great.
Now he was a singer and he also led a band for awhile?
Yes, he was a little band leader, liked to jump up and direct.
Was he sort of a musical director at the Paradise in Atlantic City?
Well I don't think he was the musical director, he was more of an entertainer.
Uh-huh.

But you know Charlie Johnson had a habit of getting up from his piano, and going out maybe somewhere, leave the band playing without a piano and he was the first one to do that and the band played very well without him. He'll do that all the time. Get up and leave the band. He'd go home, or go out and sit down, listen to his band. His band played very well without him. And maybe a guy like Half-Pint, he used to jump up there in front of the band, and clown and direct the band, that's about all.
